execSummary: Acme Analytics sells embedded usage-analytics widgets to B2B SaaS product teams. Positioning today leans on breadth of chart types rather than time-to-value, which leaves an opening against incumbents that require weeks of setup. The fastest lever is a self-serve, 15-minute-install pitch aimed at product-led growth teams currently stuck mid-implementation with a competitor.

competitors.name: MetricPilot
competitors.positioning: Enterprise-grade analytics platform with deep customization and a dedicated implementation team.
competitors.weakness: Typical implementation takes 6-8 weeks and requires a signed SOW before a customer sees a single chart, which stalls PLG-motion buyers who want to ship this quarter.

competitors.name: ChartForge
competitors.positioning: Open-source charting library with a hosted paid tier for teams that don't want to self-manage.
competitors.weakness: No built-in usage analytics or event pipeline — teams still have to build and maintain their own event tracking layer, which is the actual pain point buyers are trying to outsource.

competitors.name: InsightLoop
competitors.positioning: Analytics-as-a-feature add-on marketed primarily through app marketplace listings.
competitors.weakness: Marketplace distribution caps them to platforms they've integrated with; teams on a custom stack can't adopt them at all.

personas.name: Head of Product, Series B SaaS
personas.pain: Needs usage data to justify the next roadmap bet but engineering has no bandwidth to build internal dashboards.
personas.trigger: Just finished a board meeting where 'show me adoption numbers' came up and there was no good answer.

personas.name: Founding Engineer, seed-stage startup
personas.pain: Spending sprint time hand-rolling charts instead of shipping core product.
personas.trigger: Just shipped a v1 feature and now needs to prove usage before the next fundraising update.

personas.name: VP Customer Success
personas.pain: Can't see per-account feature adoption, so renewal conversations are guesswork.
personas.trigger: A renewal was just lost because a champion left and no one noticed the account had gone quiet.

outreach.subject: 15 minutes vs. 6 weeks
outreach.body: Hey {{FirstName}}, if you're mid-way through a MetricPilot SOW and still waiting on your first dashboard, worth knowing Acme installs in about 15 minutes with a single script tag. Happy to show you a live account if useful.

outreach.subject: For your next board deck
outreach.body: Saw {{Company}} is scaling fast — when the board asks for adoption numbers next time, do you have a fast answer? Acme gives product teams per-feature usage charts without an engineering ticket.

{{FirstName}}, most founding engineers we talk to have burned at least a sprint hand-building usage charts. Acme replaces that entirely — install once, get the dashboards your team needs without maintaining them.

outreach.subject: Catch a quiet account before it churns
outreach.body: Losing a renewal because a champion went quiet and nobody noticed is one of the most avoidable losses in CS. Acme surfaces per-account feature adoption drop-offs automatically so your team sees it before the renewal call.
No sales call required to try it — {{Company}} could have Acme running in a dev environment before this email thread ends. Want the install snippet?

If your team is maintaining a homegrown charting library on top of raw event data, that's exactly the maintenance burden Acme exists to remove. One install, and the charts + the event pipeline are both handled.

outreach.subject: Ship analytics this sprint, not next quarter
outreach.body: For product-led teams, waiting 6-8 weeks on an analytics vendor kills momentum. {{Company}} could have real usage data in the product this week instead.
If part of your stack isn't covered by the usual marketplace analytics add-ons, that's a gap Acme is built to fill — it's platform-agnostic by design, not tied to a specific app store integration.

outreach.subject: Usage numbers before your next raise
outreach.body: Investors increasingly want to see product usage, not just revenue. If {{Company}} doesn't have clean adoption charts yet, Acme can get you there before your next update goes out.
What would your eng team ship instead if they got back the time currently spent on internal dashboards? That's the trade Acme is offering — happy to talk specifics for {{Company}}'s stack.

nextMove: Ship a self-serve install flow (script tag + hosted quickstart) so a PLG-motion prospect can go from signup to first chart in under 15 minutes without a sales call, and lead outbound with a direct time-to-value comparison against MetricPilot.
